utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Call the case please, Mr. Court Deputy.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is Case Number IT-02-60-T, the Prosecutor versus Vidoje Blagojevic and Dragan Jokic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Good morning, everybody. Mr. Karnavas, are you ready for the next witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. President, Your Honours, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we have the next witness, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Would you make the solemn declaration, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You may sit down, please. Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: PERICA VASOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Would you please tell us what your name is.

utterances.speaker: PERICA VASOVIC
utterances.text: My name is Perica Vasovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Would you please tell us your last name letter by letter.

utterances.speaker: PERICA VASOVIC
utterances.text: V-a-s-o-v-i-c.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Vasovic, where are you from?

utterances.speaker: PERICA VASOVIC
utterances.text: I live in Bratunac now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: How long have you lived in Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: PERICA VASOVIC
utterances.text: Since 1984.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And before moving to Bratunac, where were you living?

utterances.speaker: PERICA VASOVIC
utterances.text: In Andrijevica in Montenegro.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Would you please tell us what your educational background is.

utterances.speaker: PERICA VASOVIC
utterances.text: I completed secondary school for economics and the higher school, the post-secondary two-year school for economics.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. What brought you to Bratunac in 1984?

utterances.speaker: PERICA VASOVIC
utterances.text: In 1984 it was because of my job, and this is where I established my family.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And what job was that?

utterances.speaker: PERICA VASOVIC
utterances.text: In the company Geosonda with its headquarters in Belgrade, which was conducting land surveying for mining purposes in Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And today where do you work?

utterances.speaker: PERICA VASOVIC
utterances.text: I am now employed in the municipal veterans organisation of Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Are you a veteran of the war yourself?

utterances.speaker: PERICA VASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, until the 14th of December, 1992. I was a soldier, then I was wounded and that was when I stopped being a member of the Army of Republika Srpska for the reason that I became a war invalid.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And after you were injured, did you perform any work known as working obligation?

utterances.speaker: PERICA VASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. From February 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: What sort of work was that?

utterances.speaker: PERICA VASOVIC
utterances.text: In the composite agricultural cooperative in Bratunac. I was in charge of logistics and the sale of agricultural products.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, I want to focus your attention to July 1995 at a period when Srebrenica fell. And as a point of reference, Srebrenica fell on 11 July 1995. Okay?

utterances.speaker: PERICA VASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Do you recall where you were and what you were doing on 11 July 1995?

utterances.speaker: PERICA VASOVIC
utterances.text: On the 11th of July, 1995, I was performing my regular work connected with the sale of raspberries in Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Well, were you working for yourself or were you working for an organisation, an enterprise?

utterances.speaker: PERICA VASOVIC
utterances.text: We were working for the composite agricultural co-op, which at the time was socially owned. So I was not working for myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And who was the director or the manager of the co-op at that point in time?

utterances.speaker: PERICA VASOVIC
utterances.text: The director was Jovan Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And he also goes by Jole. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PERICA VASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: That's his nickname. Now, where exactly were you on the 11th? Do you recall? Were you in Bratunac or were you someplace else?

utterances.speaker: PERICA VASOVIC
utterances.text: I was on the outskirts of Bratunac, because the co-op refrigerator is located on the road between Bratunac and Ljubovija. It's 1 kilometre away from the town.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, I want to focus your attention on the following day, that would be July 12th, 1995, the day after Srebrenica fell. Do you recall where you were at that time?

utterances.speaker: PERICA VASOVIC
utterances.text: In the morning, I was in the administration building of the co-op in Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Did you spend the entire morning there or did you have an opportunity to walk around the town?

utterances.speaker: PERICA VASOVIC
utterances.text: I was there in the morning after a few hours. I left in order to go to the warehouses to prepare the goods for sale for the following day.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: On that particular day, did you by any chance go to Potocari?

utterances.speaker: PERICA VASOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: On that day, do you recall any -- witnessing any particular incident that might help you as a point of reference as to whether you were in Potocari or not?

utterances.speaker: PERICA VASOVIC
utterances.text: No, no, I wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did you happen to see General Mladic that day?

utterances.speaker: PERICA VASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Would you please tell us where was it that you saw General Mladic.

utterances.speaker: PERICA VASOVIC
utterances.text: At the crossroads of the Bratunac and Srebrenica roads.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And how was it that you saw him?

utterances.speaker: PERICA VASOVIC
utterances.text: By accident. I was standing at the crossroads when he came along in his vehicle.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: What were you doing?

utterances.speaker: PERICA VASOVIC
utterances.text: I was standing there and talking to a passer-by.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And do you recall what happened?

utterances.speaker: PERICA VASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Would you please describe to us what you saw.

utterances.speaker: PERICA VASOVIC
utterances.text: The car in which the general was stopped at the crossroads. Next to me was a military policeman, whom I don't know. The general called out and ordered us to stand to attention. And he yelled at us because we were loitering about on the street. He slapped the military policeman and he ordered us to return to the unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Did you return to any unit?

utterances.speaker: PERICA VASOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't because I was not a conscript. I was unfit for military service at that point.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. On that particular day -- and if I understand you correctly, that's the 12th, the day of the fall of Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: PERICA VASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Do you recall seeing any buses in Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: PERICA VASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I did see more buses than usual than I would have seen on a normal day.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did you notice who was in the buses?

utterances.speaker: PERICA VASOVIC
utterances.text: The buses, when I saw them, were going off in the direction of Potocari.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Did you see any buses coming from Potocari going in the opposite direction?

utterances.speaker: PERICA VASOVIC
utterances.text: As I was out in the street only briefly, I didn't. I went to the raspberry warehouse, which is about a kilometre and a half away from Bratunac. And I stayed there until the evening.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, the next day, July 13th, 1995, do you recall going to Potocari?

utterances.speaker: PERICA VASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Could you please describe to us how it is that you went to Potocari.

utterances.speaker: PERICA VASOVIC
utterances.text: I went to Potocari out of curiosity, hoping to see some of my prewar friends.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. How did you get to Potocari?

utterances.speaker: PERICA VASOVIC
utterances.text: I can't say exactly what time it was, but it was around 10.00 or 10.30. Jovan Nikolic, known as Jole, came along, he came by.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Was he with anyone?

utterances.speaker: PERICA VASOVIC
utterances.text: He was with Momir Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Were they walking by?

utterances.speaker: PERICA VASOVIC
utterances.text: They were in a Zastava vehicle, a 101. I can't remember what colour it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And then what?

utterances.speaker: PERICA VASOVIC
utterances.text: Stojan Ilic and I were chatting at the crossroads and standing there. And then Nikolic, both of them, stopped in their vehicle next to us. We asked them where they were going. And they said they were going to Potocari to see what was going on there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. What happened after that?

utterances.speaker: PERICA VASOVIC
utterances.text: We asked whether they could give us a lift and they agreed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And then what?

utterances.speaker: PERICA VASOVIC
utterances.text: We got into the car and set out toward Potocari.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Was there any conversation on the way to Potocari that you can recollect today?

utterances.speaker: PERICA VASOVIC
utterances.text: The usual kind of conversation. We heard from Momir that the Army of Republika Srpska had entered Srebrenica, and that the people had set out toward the federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. When you got to Potocari, what did you do?

utterances.speaker: PERICA VASOVIC
utterances.text: After the first checkpoint when we were among the people, we stopped and got out. And each of us talked to somebody individually. There were loads of people there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Did you happen to notice what Momir Nikolic was doing?

utterances.speaker: PERICA VASOVIC
utterances.text: Momir Nikolic was talking to those people, saying hello.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did Momir Nikolic ever tell you whether he had a particular function there?

utterances.speaker: PERICA VASOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did he ever say to you that he had been appointed by the Main Staff as the coordinator of all the tasks?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: I think we had a similar situation yesterday. He was asked before whether he had a particular function -- whether Momir Nikolic told him whether he had a particular function, the witness said no. And the follow-up question is entirely leading, and I don't think it's helpful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, we have heard a lot of witnesses who testified on this subject. And in these circumstances maybe the witness did not understand what the particular function means. So I think it doesn't matter for the Defence counsel to be more specific. But it is indeed a leading question. Mr. Karnavas, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did Momir Nikolic ever tell you whether he had an important role to play in the evacuation the day before?

utterances.speaker: PERICA VASOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did he mention any -- receiving any orders from a Colonel Jankovic of the Main Staff?

utterances.speaker: PERICA VASOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did he tell you about some conversation that he might have had with an individual named Popovic or Kosoric?

utterances.speaker: PERICA VASOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did you see him give any orders while he was there to any commanders of any units that might have been there at the time carrying out any activities?

utterances.speaker: PERICA VASOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't see him give any orders.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If you could just please tell us from your observations what you believed, at the time, Momir Nikolic was doing there.

utterances.speaker: PERICA VASOVIC
utterances.text: I thought he had come there out of curiosity, just like the three of us.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Did anyone come up to Momir Nikolic seeking advice, consultation, with respect to needs of coordination of units, buses, trucks, individuals?

utterances.speaker: PERICA VASOVIC
utterances.text: No. He paid more attention to the people, saying hello, chatting to them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. So I take it Momir Nikolic knew some of those individuals that were there?

utterances.speaker: PERICA VASOVIC
utterances.text: Momir Nikolic was a teacher before the war so that many people knew him, his former students, parents of students. And it was probably those people that he was shaking hands with and saying hello to.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. How long did you stay in Potocari, if you recall?

utterances.speaker: PERICA VASOVIC
utterances.text: In my estimation, some 15 or 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And from Potocari, where did you go?

utterances.speaker: PERICA VASOVIC
utterances.text: We returned to Bratunac by the same route.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, when you say "we," who is we?

utterances.speaker: PERICA VASOVIC
utterances.text: Momir Nikolic, Jovan Nikolic, Stojan Ilic, and I.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And where did you go -- when you returned to Bratunac, where did you -- what did you do?

utterances.speaker: PERICA VASOVIC
utterances.text: We got out at the crossroads where the administration building was, and Momir went to the command of the Bratunac Brigade, or so he said.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did he, by any chance, tell you why he was going there?

utterances.speaker: PERICA VASOVIC
utterances.text: It was his duty to be at the brigade. That's probably the reason, as a soldier, an officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: From your observations, did it appear that he was -- that there was a sense of urgency on his part to get to the brigade and perhaps make some sort of a reporting as to what he had seen and observed in Potocari?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Waespi.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: I think it's again entirely leading, all these buzz words obviously important for the Defence to put into that question. He can ask - if I can give my counsel advice today - how he appeared to be when he went to the -- in what shape and form when he went to the brigade. That would be a proper question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karnavas. Put your question another way.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well. Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: From your observations of Momir Nikolic, would you please tell us how or in which fashion he went to the brigade command post.

utterances.speaker: PERICA VASOVIC
utterances.text: He wasn't in a hurry. He even invited us for coffee in the town, but we refused because we had work to do in the administration building of the co-op.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did he ever mention during that period of time that he had to meet with Colonel Blagojevic?

utterances.speaker: PERICA VASOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did he ever mention that he at any point in time had been keeping Colonel Blagojevic abreast, informed, as to his whereabouts and what he had been doing?

utterances.speaker: PERICA VASOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Witness, what do you mean by no? You mean you don't know or Mr. Momir Nikolic did not inform his boss, Mr. Blagojevic? I need an explanation.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He didn't say anything to us, nor did he let us know that he was to report to Colonel Blagojevic. I'm referring to the three of us who were with him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I believe the question was: Did he ever mention, so I wasn't implying whether he had or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. So after this encounter with Momir Nikolic, what did you do?

utterances.speaker: PERICA VASOVIC
utterances.text: I went back to the co-op warehouse, because that evening the sale of raspberries was to take place.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, since we're on Momir Nikolic, and before we get to the next day, could you tell us whether you know Momir Nikolic and how well you know him.

utterances.speaker: PERICA VASOVIC
utterances.text: I have known Momir Nikolic since 1985, and I know him quite well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And when you say "quite well," were you friends?

utterances.speaker: PERICA VASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, because his wife was from Montenegro, and because of that we grew quite close.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Did you know his parents as well?

utterances.speaker: PERICA VASOVIC
utterances.text: I was on very good terms with his father. We were very good friends, even better than with Momir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Have you stayed in touch with Momir since he has been arrested?

utterances.speaker: PERICA VASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And how?

utterances.speaker: PERICA VASOVIC
utterances.text: He sent me a postcard.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, Mr. Waespi.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Yes. If we could go into private session for a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We'll go to private session, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, while we're still on Momir Nikolic, you indicated that you know him since 1985, so I take it from your long association with him, nearly 20 years, you would have a pretty good understanding of his character?

utterances.speaker: PERICA VASOVIC
utterances.text: Since we frequently socialised and after the war were involved in similar activities, taking care of families and so on, I have been able to create an opinion about him and I believe that many people in Bratunac share my opinion.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Could you tell us what your opinion is?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Yes, I think that's a totally appropriate question, but I would like to remind counsel of yesterday when he proposed a few character traits to the witness and asked him, you know, is he a person like that. And I don't -- I would object to a question like that. This one is certainly appropriate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I believe Mr. Karnavas already bore in mind the objections you made yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I appreciate the pre-emptive admonition from my colleague. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: So could you please share with us your understanding of Momir Nikolic's character.

utterances.speaker: PERICA VASOVIC
utterances.text: Well, Momir Nikolic never displayed such features with respect to me, but however he always was a conceited person and had a superiority complex, which is the reason why he frequently had conflicts with the residents of Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And can you comment, can you comment, as to your belief or your understanding as to his character with respect to truth and honesty.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: I would like to draw the Court's attention to what the witness just said. He said: "Momir Nikolic never displayed such features with respect to me," and then he goes on. So if everything -- all he can say is what he heard about that is very limited. Especially when we now when we go into character traits with respect to truth and honesty, of which the Trial Chamber could satisfy itself when Mr. Momir Nikolic testified.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I've laid a foundation. He knows him. Just because Momir Nikolic was not arrogant, abrasive, a braggadocio, and so on and so forth with this particular gentleman, if he was able to witness it when Momir Nikolic was conducting himself in that manner, for this individual to draw these conclusions with respect to Momir Nikolic's character, he's truly qualified to comment on that. And the second question is different from the first. It is not leading; it is perfectly fine. And as far as I understand the rules of evidence, character evidence is admissible, as long as you establish a foundation. And so, I believe we have the foundation. He can say he doesn't know, he does know. But I think he's known the individual for 20 years. It's a small community. He's had lots of contact with him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas, you may proceed with your question, but we also will bear in mind the objections from the Prosecution on this issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Sir, could you please comment as to your understanding of Mr. Nikolic's character with respect to truth and honesty. Is he a truthful and honest person, your belief.

utterances.speaker: PERICA VASOVIC
utterances.text: I was able to make conclusions about his truthfulness and honesty, only after the war has ended. During the war, I had no opportunity to be in his vicinity; I had no opportunity to socialise with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And what conclusions were you able to draw after the war?

utterances.speaker: PERICA VASOVIC
utterances.text: As I was involved in taking care of Serb refugees, the ones who had fled Sarajevo municipality, I had frequent contacts with Momir Nikolic in the Ministry for Refugees and Deported Persons, where he worked in Bratunac. We had a lot of needy families, disabled persons, and homeless persons. It was difficult for me to cooperate with him and to find mutual ground, even though by law he was duty-bound to take care of these needy persons. Many families who went to see him, seeking assistance, seeking accommodation, were not successful in their requests because he always lied to them, and we had tremendous problems with him in that regard, our service did. Sometimes when he was supposed to help someone, he would even take my opinion into account more than he took into account the rules of the organisation. This reflects an unstable character. And through three years of cooperation, I know there are a hundred or more people in Bratunac who could confirm this, because he caused them harm and difficulties without reason. When he left the department Ministry for Refugees and Displaced Persons, his successor managed to take care of the most needy categories of people very quickly and in a very good way.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you, sir. Now, I just want to draw your -- I want to go back to where we left off before we began speaking about Momir Nikolic. The following -- so we -- and we were discussing the events of the 13th of July, 1995. Now, if you could tell us if you recall the following day, July 14th, 1995.

utterances.speaker: PERICA VASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Would you please tell us what, if anything, unusual happened that day that sticks out in your mind today.

utterances.speaker: PERICA VASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: PERICA VASOVIC
utterances.text: On that day, in view of the fact that I'm not from the area near the village of Kravica, which has a lot of raspberry orchards, I did not receive a report, either in writing or orally, as to what had been done at the sales point. The raspberries from this village were to have been delivered to the cooler on the 13th in the evening, but they failed to arrive. In the morning I set out toward Kravica in order to see why no report had been submitted and what our employees there were doing. As I did not have a car, I got a lift from someone from the village of Popovici. I don't remember the person's name. This is a little hamlet in the hills near Kravica. And he dropped me off about 200 metres away from the warehouse. He turned off toward his home, and I got out of the car and set out on foot toward the warehouse. As I was approaching the co-op warehouse, I heard gunfire. And I saw some unknown persons in camouflage uniforms. Out of fear for my life, I went into the first house in the village, which is across the road from the warehouse at a distance of about 100 metres. I sat down with the person whose home it was, and he said: "Don't go near there or you may lose your life." After a while, I saw a vehicle in which there was Dragan Nikolic, a war invalid, and Jovan Nikolic, also known as Jole. And they went toward the warehouse compound. As there was no fence around the warehouse because it had been taken down during the war, a few of the villagers who were in the house and myself set out toward the warehouse. Jovan Nikolic was yelling and shouting at the soldiers who were there. One of the soldiers cocked his rifle and pointed it at him. An elderly man, whose last name is Milanovic and his first name is Sveto, and Jovan was his best man, his kum, and he was afraid for his life so he begged the soldiers not to kill him. Then the soldiers turned on this elderly man, who is almost senile. To save him, Nikolic put this man into his car and took him home. The warehouses had been broken into and looted. For reasons of personal safety and the safety of the other people who were there, I did not dare object. While I was inspecting the warehouse inside, because there were a lot of goods in there, Jovan Nikolic went back to Bratunac, but I don't know who with. I didn't notice that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, sir, did you recognise these men that were carrying out these executions?

utterances.speaker: PERICA VASOVIC
utterances.text: No. They had masks.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did you recognise any of the voices?

utterances.speaker: PERICA VASOVIC
utterances.text: I talked to three soldiers who were in the canteen and I asked them what they were doing. I was astonished. I was horrified. They exchanged a few words with me. This was a soldier who was not wearing a mask, but I didn't know him. Neither of these two had masks on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Did you ask them where they were from?

utterances.speaker: PERICA VASOVIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't ask them where they were from, but they didn't seem to be local people. They appeared to be soldiers from the area of Sarajevo because they were mixing up the sounds č and ć. This is characteristic of that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: So from their pronunciation of certain words, you believed that they might have been from another area?

utterances.speaker: PERICA VASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I was able to observe that all people who come from the Sarajevo area confuse these two sounds č and ć. The refugees now living in Bratunac from that area all speak like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Well, sir, I don't have any more questions at this time. Thank you very much. I believe Mr. Stojanovic may have some questions and the Prosecution and the Judges may also have questions of you. I would appreciate if you would be as frank and as forthcoming with them as you have been with me. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Stojanovic, do you have any questions to this witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. We have no questions for this witness, in view of his testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, Mr. Waespi, maybe we could have an early break. And when we resume, you will begin your cross-examination. So we will break until 20 minutes to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Waespi, your cross-examination, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Vasovic.

utterances.speaker: PERICA VASOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: I only have a few questions for you this morning, and it won't take long.

utterances.speaker: PERICA VASOVIC
utterances.text: Just go ahead. Go ahead, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Can you tell me your father's name.

utterances.speaker: PERICA VASOVIC
utterances.text: Dragomir.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Now, are you on the roster of members of the Bratunac Brigade in July 1995? Would that be a possibility?

utterances.speaker: PERICA VASOVIC
utterances.text: No. I was not on the roster because -- shall I explain?

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: PERICA VASOVIC
utterances.text: Because I was wounded in 1992 on the 14th of December. I underwent treatment in the Zvornik health centre, the VMA, and in the rehabilitation centre Banja Kovaljaca. I was declared unfit for military service and therefore I could no longer be a member of the brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Was it possible that in 1995 you received some sort of benefits from the Bratunac Brigade because or despite the fact that you were unfit or disabled, as you told us?

utterances.speaker: PERICA VASOVIC
utterances.text: War invalids get their income from a certain fund, which still exists today, not from the brigade or the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Okay. Let me then show you a document.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, it's exhibit P165. If the witness could be shown. And, Mr. President, the only relevant page is the second-to-last page, and we do have a translation of the heading and the titles. It's a list of names, as you will see. And perhaps the witness can tell us whether he recognises his name on this list. And I think we can put it on to the ELMO, the B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Mr. Vasovic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Waespi, is that document under seal?

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, if it's under seal, please do not put it on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: You're right. I do apologise for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: So if you would just go over the document --

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Perhaps out of an abundance of caution if we could go into private session so --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we'll go to private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Now, a few questions about Kravica, 14th July. You told us you were present that day. Did you see -- when you approached the warehouse, did you see bodies there?

utterances.speaker: PERICA VASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And how many bodies did you see there?

utterances.speaker: PERICA VASOVIC
utterances.text: I couldn't say how many, but there was a pile of bodies. I didn't come near them and I couldn't do that anyway.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: I thought you said you -- later on you went with Jovan Nikolic to these, as they were described, executioners --

utterances.speaker: PERICA VASOVIC
utterances.text: I came up to the building when they attacked Jovan Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Okay. Have you heard that these bodies from Kravica were dumped at a site in Glogova?

utterances.speaker: PERICA VASOVIC
utterances.text: No. I didn't hear it on that day and nobody mentioned it. Later on I heard this from the people, from rumours going around the town.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Now, do you know an area called Ravnice just very close to the warehouse?

utterances.speaker: PERICA VASOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Have you heard of a little hamlet called Adzici in the same area on the road, Bratunac-Konjevic Polje, just above the road. It's very close to the main road?

utterances.speaker: PERICA VASOVIC
utterances.text: Adzici?

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Yes. It's in the village of Halilovici, Glogova.

utterances.speaker: PERICA VASOVIC
utterances.text: No. I know about Halilovici. There's a signpost saying Halilovici, but I'm not really familiar with that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: So you heard later about the bodies of the Glogova. Have you heard in this little hamlet, Ravnice, 200 bodies were dumped to the street? Have you heard about these two things as well?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm going to object on the grounds of relevancy. Unless counsel can now establish some foundation as to why this is relevant with respect to this particular witness. I do object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I think some questions asked in the cross-examination may have some relevance to the case, or in the cross-examination the Prosecution or the parties could ask any questions which goes to the credibility of this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: You may proceed, Mr. Waespi.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: So you said you had heard about the bodies in Glogova?

utterances.speaker: PERICA VASOVIC
utterances.text: That's what I heard, but I didn't go there. I never went there, nor do I know where this is.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And -- so you don't know where these dump sites were, these graves who were dug those days in Glogova? You still don't know that today.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Objection. That's not what the witness said, and now we're getting into an area where he's trying to be unfair with the witness. He never said that he's unaware of it today. I think it's -- he's being unfair to the witness, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I believe the Prosecution is just making sure what the answer of this witness is.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Yes, I apologise if there was a misunderstanding. I believe the witness said he still doesn't know where the graves are. And I apologise. If that's not correct, the witness can clarify the point.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Do you know today where these graves in Glogova are?

utterances.speaker: PERICA VASOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Let me turn to another subject. Do you know the Red Berets of the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: PERICA VASOVIC
utterances.text: I heard about them, but I didn't see them. As I was wounded quite early on, I spent a long time undergoing treatment.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Do you know any members of the Red Berets?

utterances.speaker: PERICA VASOVIC
utterances.text: I know the late Bosko Neskovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Anybody else?

utterances.speaker: PERICA VASOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't know them. They were younger than me, not my generation. So I didn't know them well.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: So if you saw any member of these Red Berets, you wouldn't be able to place them into this Red Beret unit. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PERICA VASOVIC
utterances.text: Seen them where?

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: For instance, Kravica.

utterances.speaker: PERICA VASOVIC
utterances.text: I would recognise their faces, their physical appearance. I knew what they looked like, but I didn't know their names.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Do you know Miroslav Stanojevic, the way he looks like?

utterances.speaker: PERICA VASOVIC
utterances.text: Miroslav Stanojevic, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: So you don't know -- yes?

utterances.speaker: PERICA VASOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: You have never heard of him?

utterances.speaker: PERICA VASOVIC
utterances.text: There are many people called Stanojevic in Bratunac, but I don't know Miroslav.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: You are hesitating. Maybe you have heard that he was wounded in Kravica?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I object to that commentary that he's hesitating. It could be that he's waiting for the translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Maybe there is a procedural issue. We still have a lot of time, and there is no need for haste.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Yes. Do you want to clarify anything, Mr. Vasovic?

utterances.speaker: PERICA VASOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know Miroslav Stanovic and I didn't hear that he was wounded in Kravica.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Did you hear that he was killed in Kravica?

utterances.speaker: PERICA VASOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know that he was killed in Kravica. Had he been killed, his picture would have been brought to the memorial room but so far nobody has brought a picture of him to be put in the memorial room and I haven't seen him. But maybe he didn't have any family to do that. Anyway, I didn't hear about this.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Have you heard that he was killed in a car accident later on?

utterances.speaker: PERICA VASOVIC
utterances.text: No. I don't know him. There's nothing I can say about him.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Let me go to the last point. You told us today that you were frightened when you approached the warehouse and heard the shots. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PERICA VASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And you feared for your life?

utterances.speaker: PERICA VASOVIC
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And I think you testified even that somebody local there told you not to go there because it's dangerous?

utterances.speaker: PERICA VASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And then you witnessed a heavy exchange between Jovan Nikolic and these, as we heard, executioners. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PERICA VASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And still afterwards you went to the canteen and had coffee with these executioners. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PERICA VASOVIC
utterances.text: No. I found them in the room where there was no electricity, no water, let alone coffee. Why would I be drinking coffee with them?

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: But you talked to them?

utterances.speaker: PERICA VASOVIC
utterances.text: In passing, yes. I asked who had broken into my warehouse and the premises and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Did you ask them about whether they killed these many, many bodies you had seen there?

utterances.speaker: PERICA VASOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: So the only thing you were concerned was who has broken into your warehouse and the premises and so on?

utterances.speaker: PERICA VASOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, I wouldn't even dare ask them. I was naturally concerned, wasn't interested in the warehouse or anything else. However, I didn't dare -- I didn't dare.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Did you see some heavy machinery standing there while you were at Kravica warehouse?

utterances.speaker: PERICA VASOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. No further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Any re-direct?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If we could get the assistance of the usher for that exhibit that was shown by the Prosecutor, the roster.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Shall we go into private session?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: That won't be necessary, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If you could just look at that, sir. I just want to clarify a couple of points. And of course I believe there are other documents there with respect to that roster. Now, at that time - we're talking July 1995 - were you a member of the 3rd Battalion of the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: PERICA VASOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Prior to you getting wounded, were you a member of the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: PERICA VASOVIC
utterances.text: I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And do you recall which unit you were serving in when you were a member of the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: PERICA VASOVIC
utterances.text: The 1st Company, 3rd Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And some of the other names that you see there, do you recall whether they were also the ones that you indicated that they were also invalids --

utterances.speaker: PERICA VASOVIC
utterances.text: I know all of these people.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I don't want to -- we don't need to mention any names. But my question is: Do you recall whether they were members of that battalion as well?

utterances.speaker: PERICA VASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, in various units.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And was there not a practice, sir, that by having your name on a roster such as this one, provisions could be provided for the family members?

utterances.speaker: PERICA VASOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Can I clarify something, sir?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes. But again, if you do not mention any particular name that's on there.

utterances.speaker: PERICA VASOVIC
utterances.text: This document is very clear, very explicit. We received assistance from the brigade. It says here: "For the provisions, for the supplies," and the signatures on the side are those of neighbours, spouses, and so on. I can see here that somebody picked up supplies that had been assigned to me. I didn't pick them myself, but by the signatures, there is a clarification, whether it was a neighbor, a sister, a wife.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Do you recognise that signature that's next to your name?

utterances.speaker: PERICA VASOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And prior to coming here today and being shown this document, had you seen this document?

utterances.speaker: PERICA VASOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, let me move on to the next issue, and that's the Kravica incident. Now, are you clear you were there on that particular day and you saw those people committing those executions?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: I don't know what the purpose is in re-examination. I --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: It's not re-examination, Your Honour. There seems to be -- the Prosecution seems to be on the knife edge deciding whether he witnessed them or not. He's trying somehow to discredit the individual that he did not see the killings. Or if he did see the killings, afterwards he was dispassionate and had coffee with them. So I don't know how that fits into the theory of their case, but nonetheless they are attacking the gentleman's credibility and honesty with respect to what he witnessed and what he did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I think some matters we heard yesterday corroborated with the testimony of this witness. So since some questions have already been asked in the direct examination and the cross-examination, I believe there is no need to repeat them. The re-direct examination should be within the scope of the cross-examination. I hope you bear that in mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I am bearing that in mind.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, you were asked about a particular individual, whether you knew him, whether you heard of his name, Miroslav Stanojevic. I believe you indicated that you did not know him. Correct?

utterances.speaker: PERICA VASOVIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: But did I hear you clearly that if you would have seen the face of someone that you recognised, you would at least be able to tell us that you recognised someone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Waespi.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Mr. President, that's entirely leading.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'll rephrase, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: No, no, I don't think so. I believe that the witness told us about that. But you could put your question another way.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'll put it another way.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did you recognise any of the faces of those individuals that did not have a mask on?

utterances.speaker: PERICA VASOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, with respect to Glogova, were you involved at all in the burial process of Glogova?

utterances.speaker: PERICA VASOVIC
utterances.text: No. Why would somebody engage me in that kind of effort when there was no need for that?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Could you please explain to us what reasons might you have for concealing information as to where the graves in Glogova would be while at the same time telling us that you witnessed ongoing executions?

utterances.speaker: PERICA VASOVIC
utterances.text: There would be no reasons for that. Had I seen it, I would have said so, where they were buried or any other information.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: You were asked a question with respect to the people that you did speak to. Why didn't you ask them who killed the Muslims that were there, that pile of bodies that you saw. I'm not quite clear as to why you didn't ask them who killed those Muslims. So could you please clarify your answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: I believe the witness said: "I was afraid." So I don't see the...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We believe that question is asked and answered.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If that is the objection, Your Honour, and if the Prosecution is satisfied with the answer, then I'll -- I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Karnavas. Yes, Judge Argibay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ARGIBAY
utterances.text: Good morning, sir. I have one question for you. When you were reading this postcard you received. And we are in open session, I won't mention especially the thing. You said that when it was referring to "traitors," you believed that to be mention of Mr. Deronjic. Can you tell me why.

utterances.speaker: PERICA VASOVIC
utterances.text: Before coming to the Detention Unit, on one occasion when we were together, the two of us, he said that should he go to The Hague, Miroslav would follow very soon thereafter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ARGIBAY
utterances.text: And what has that to do with the word "traitor"? I don't understand you, if you can explain it.

utterances.speaker: PERICA VASOVIC
utterances.text: They had some accounts to settle between them, privately. And they were arguing and discussing things between them. And he would frequently inform me about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ARGIBAY
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I have got a question. Witness, are you sure that you were in Potocari with the other people, including Momir Nikolic, on the 12th of July instead of the 13th of July?

utterances.speaker: PERICA VASOVIC
utterances.text: I'm sure it was on the 13th. I know where I was on the 12th. The meeting with the general, that short meeting with the general, is very clear in my mind. Therefore, I got lost in order not to be there in his company.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Are there any questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Perhaps if I could assist, I think, the Rule 65 ter summaries wasn't clear and perhaps your question is based on that account.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Any questions out of the Judges' questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. I believe I did make a notation in the previous proofing notes, noting that the error was on my part and not the witness's. But I have no further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. At this stage, are there any documents to tender? Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, just to be on the safe side, I would like to tender the postcard. And I do have a -- we are waiting for the official translation to come, you know, any day now. It's been in there for several days, in fact weeks. But that would be the only document. I believe that would be D123/1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well -- well, Mr. Karnavas, I'm not sure whether we should admit it into the evidence or not at this stage, because so far as I know you read all the contents of that postcard into the transcript. Do you think we still need to admit it? Maybe for some stamps? The dates? I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I think the -- it is quite difficult to read the actual date. So I think that the original should come in. I have spoken with the gentleman here, and he's made a copy of it for his own records. And he's -- as I understand it, he's willing to part with the original postcard.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. This document, D123/1, is admitted into the evidence, pending the official translation, which means if there are any problems the parties, the other party has the right to challenge the translation of that postcard. And it is admitted under seal. Thank you. Yes, as for this postcard, we still have a question, that is on which year at least this witness received that postcard. Could we ask the witness to answer that question?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Of course. Would you like me to ask it or --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Maybe you could ask it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Sir, do you recall which year you received the postcard?

utterances.speaker: PERICA VASOVIC
utterances.text: I only know that when Momir came to The Hague and then his wife, Dusanka, went to visit him, some 10 to 15 days after that I received the postcard.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Do you know whether it was before or after he entered into his bargain with the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: PERICA VASOVIC
utterances.text: I think that it was before, at least by media -- following the media accounts of it. I think it was much before that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, thank you very much indeed for your coming to The Hague to give your evidence. We appreciate it very much.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: When the hearing is adjourned, the usher will show you out of the room. We wish you a pleasant journey back home. As I said yesterday that we will spend some time on the procedural matters, which could be called a Status Conference. And we will adjourn for 15 minutes for everybody to get the necessary materials and documents concerning of the 65 ter filings by the Defence counsel. So the hearing is adjourned until half past 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
